title: Reduce mixed line/hyperplane recharts to two-bit closure (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration, produced by Nick Petalas. Mixed common-line/hyperplane recharts with dimension-linear signed prices admit an exact maximum-closure reduction over every field.

```text
U intersect H, U, (U intersect H)+L, U+L
    -> one or two Boolean bits per helper
nesting -> at most four implications per original edge
linear vertex/rank-gap prices + fixed options -> one minimum cut
```

Here H is one common hyperplane and L one common transverse line. The graph has at most 2N Boolean nodes and 4E nesting implications. A complete small example has original rank gap 1, growth-only optimum 2, shrinkage-only optimum 2 and mixed optimum 3. Two scope examples show that strict positive-rank feasibility need not be implication-closed, and that a power tariff does not become a unary linear bit objective. This is an optimization-interface result, with no new kappa, emitted physical word, supplier admission or selected-frontier change.

ToikY #7459 at `4f3dc4a40e2a3bee5fc0d6d5dfd7e4e95614fc22` supplies the mixed-growth/demotion opening and retains its #7456/#7454/#7334/#7113 lineage. David Ganz / Dugongue #556 already gives a different binary U/oblique-projection cut theorem, including monotone nonlinear paid prices. Its theorem is pinned as background. No predecessor executable, numerical bound, construction or receipt is replayed or imported. Maximum closure/min-cut and distributive lattices are classical; the new claim is the explicit mixed two-bit representation and its exact linear-price consequence. New work is Apache-2.0.

## Evidence

Before, the mixed family leaves up to four choices at each helper, outside the separate one-sided screens. After, direct containment and the implication encoding agree on every one of 552,408 option pairs across all subspaces and transverse hyperplane/line flags of F2 dimensions 2 through 4. The certificate enumerates 154 flags, 8,518 local lattices and 63,480 nested edges.

Independent direct enumeration of subspace assignments agrees with the cut optimizer on 1,950 signed integer price cases, 548 rational-price fixed-option cases and 83 graph/cycle cases. Eight invalid-domain controls require exact rejection reasons. Normal and optimized registered checks pass. Each direct check takes under one second locally; the read-only exported runs took 0.30 seconds each on CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64. These are replay-budget measurements, not a performance improvement claim.

Exact committed bytes, modes and declared source history pass. Official export creation/integrity checks and read-only Git-free normal/optimized replays with empty executable PATH pass. The generated six-file SHA256 receipts agree across modes. Source compilation passes, all functions are at most 34 lines, and no generated files remain in the checkout.

Reproduce from the repository root. Other machines may substitute their CPython 3.12 path.

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/mixed-rechart-closure/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/mixed-rechart-closure/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/mixed-rechart-closure
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/mixed-rechart-closure --check-source-history --check-modes
```

## Limitations

The all-field claim is the written proof; finite binary checks corroborate it. Zero edge rank gaps are allowed. Nonlinear signed power tariffs, strict productive-rank constraints, distinct independent rechart directions and physical realization are outside the reduction. The power example excludes a unary linear rewrite; it does not exclude richer pairwise cut constructions.

No actual P104 word is optimized. A supplier application still owes a complete current edge inventory, scalar/native legality, endpoint contracts, positive productive ranks, ownership, dirty restoration, precision, stock and full fees. All five framework assumptions remain. No selected scientific cold replay, predecessor scientific suite, Lean or Docker run was performed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

- Derive an exact optimization or useful certified bound for the nonlinear signed invoice on this mixed lattice, starting with one paid/productive edge's mixed differences and positive-rank constraints.
- Bind one current P104 public-component inventory and complete endpoint/incident-edge contract before searching for a physically legal gain. The abstract rank-gap example supplies no such invoice.

## Related open work

- #7459 is the source question and common-hyperplane-only screen. This proves a mixed-family linear optimization lemma and does not recompute its bounds.
- #7456 allows common-vector growth with productive endpoint credits. This permits growth and demotion together under the stated linear-price relaxation.
- #7454 fixes endpoints for common-vector growth. Fixed allowed endpoint choices are included here.
- #7458 checks selected common two-plane growth directions. The present family fixes one transverse line/hyperplane pair.
- #7453 checks individual current multi-ADD components with fixed endpoints. This lemma permits simultaneous abstract nested choices and does not assert literal scalar legality.
- #7334 supplies a current physical word used by those screens. This package does not modify or optimize it.

The completion check inspected this account's seven other open PRs created since the advance CLAIM: #7461, #7462, #7463, #7464, #7466, #7467 and #7468. They concern quadratic-refinement widths, a selected binary map, an A1 projector denominator, compiler plateau widths, robust pairing capacity, an A1 multiplicity operator and tensor-prefix scales. None studies this mixed rechart family or computes its closure/rank-gap optimum. No additional mathematical comparison was run.

## CI notes

**CI did not certify this package.** At unchanged head `a1b1b327a0780b3ec12c4aa02586487c017e1256`, [run 43279933171](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43279933171), [plan job 131398194664](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43279933171/job/131398194664), failed in `Onboarding helper tests`. I read the actual job log: 760 tests, exactly one failure, 24 skipped. The failing test is `test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`; its AssertionError says `` `make frontier7000-verify` `` was not found in the CI verification document.

The mismatch is already present on base main `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`: `certificates/selected-result.json` names `make frontier7000-verify`, while `docs/ci-verification.md` still describes #6030 and `make frontier6030-verify`. Both base files were inspected. This PR changes neither file nor the failing test. The [package replay job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43279933171/job/131400942246) was skipped because plan failed.

I also read the failed-job logs for [run 42905094314](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905094314/job/130140894651), [run 42903313790](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42903313790/job/130134720799) and [run 43280276547](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43280276547/job/131399411966). Each has the same sole failing test, missing-command assertion, 760-test total and 24 skips. This establishes a shared repository-level CI blocker and supplies no hosted mathematical coverage for this package. All package verification evidence above remains local.

No fix, retrigger commit, push or workflow rerun was made. Repair of main remains with maintainers.

## Merge danger

Two-way door. Blast radius: isolated. Six new files under research/mixed-rechart-closure; no selected record, shared implementation or frozen source is changed.
